doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later Blue Note years and ending the habit
title: Roy Haynes replaces Tony and favorite drummers
summary: McLean praises Haynes as in Tony's roots and lists Carvin, Burrage, Eric McPherson, Nasheet Waits and Louis Nash.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Tony goes out, and Roy Haynes comes in, playing in the same configuration. Did that change things?
Roy is so great. Roy Haynes is like at the seed somewhere. He’s in there in Tony’s roots somewhere. Tony’s roots go down, and you find Roy Haynes under there in the soil.
Do you think Roy had to change his playing to operate in what you were trying to do?

No, uh-uh, no, man. He’s open to that. Roy is an exceptional drummer, great, great drummer. One of my favorites. There’s so many drummers that I’m in love with, like Michael Carvin and Ronnie Burrage. Of course Eric is my latest, and then there’s Nasheet Waits. Nasheet is bad. Louis Nash is another one of my favorite drummers. I love Louis Nash.
